correctness.rationale: For a fixed rank-\(r\) projection, conjugation gives the diagonal block form and every rank-one idempotent is an outer product with a normalized pairing. The commutator splits into two off-diagonal rank-one blocks, and \(C^3=lpha(lpha-1)C\) determines the exact similarity types including nilpotent Jordan boundaries. Dot-product fibers of sizes \(U_m\) and \(W_m\) yield all seven table entries, summing to \(q^{n-1}(q^n-1)/(q-1)\). The finite standalone verifier independently enumerates fields and verifies each cell plus the cubic law; unrestricted claims follow from the proof.

originality.rationale: The claim is the rank-one/interior-rank joint product-trace and commutator-similarity distribution, plus an exact rank-dependent asymptotic law. An existing special case fixes both ranks at one; inspected primary literature counts single left-ideal generators or asks only existence of commuting class representatives. Actual mathematical-record searches did not reveal stronger coverage. This assessment is relative to inspected literature, not a guarantee of first publication.

value.rationale: The product trace detects the algebraic powers through \((PQ)^2=lpha PQ\), whereas the rational-canonical type of \(PQ-QP\) quantifies the compatibility defect. The complete table treats every finite field and every interior rank \(2\le r\le n-2\), yielding a rank-dependent binomial limit and a mixed-dimension concentration law. These are natural intrinsic joint matrix-pair invariants, rather than small-case recomputations. No conclusion for two arbitrary interior-rank factors is asserted.
